'''John Richard Pyke''' (born 28 August 1940) is an Australian [[physicist]] and a former university law [[lecturer]].<ref name=qut>{{cite web 
  | title =John Pyke - Faculty of Law 
  | publisher =[[Queensland University of Technology]] 
  | url =http://staff.qut.edu.au/staff/pyke/ 
  | accessdate =11 February 2012 
  | archive-date =2 February 2012 
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20120202000357/http://staff.qut.edu.au/staff/pyke 
  | url-status =dead 
  }}</ref> In retirement he still writes about [[Constitutional Law]].<ref>[http://legal.thomsonreuters.com.au/government-powers-under-a-federal-constitution-constitutional-law-in-australia/productdetail/125093 Government Powers under a Federal Constitution: Constitutional Law in Australia] Retrieved 17 February 2017.</ref> He was a [[Queensland]] [[Senate of Australia|Senate]] candidate at the [[Candidates of the 2001 Australian federal election|2001]] and [[Candidates of the 2010 Australian federal election|2010 Australian Federal Election]].<ref name=qsc>{{cite web
  | title =John Richard Pyke, Queensland Senate candidate, 2010 Federal Election
  | publisher =My Sunshine Coast
  | url =http://www.mysunshinecoast.com.au/business/display/john-richard-pyke-queensland-senate-candidate-2010-federal-election,38269,2837
  | accessdate = 11 February 2012}}</ref>

==Family==
Pyke was born in [[Melbourne, Victoria]], the first son of three children born to educator [[Lawrence Pyke]] and his wife Mavis (née Clarke).<ref name=family>{{cite web
  | title =Pyke Family Tree
  | publisher =Polyplex
  | url =http://polyplex.org/family/lrdp0.htm
  | accessdate = 11 February 2012}}</ref> He is the grandson of the teacher, journalist  and author, [[Lillian Pyke|Lillian Maxwell Pyke]] (1881–1927).<ref name=adb>{{cite web
  | title =Pyke, Lillian Maxwell (1881–1927)
  | publisher =[[Australian Dictionary of Biography]] 
  | url =https://adb.anu.edu.au/biography/pyke-lillian-maxwell-13161
  | access-date = 11 February 2012}}</ref>

==Education==
From 1952 until 1957, Pyke was educated at [[Newington College]],<ref>Newington College Register of Past Students 1863-1998 (Syd, 1999) pp161</ref>  where his father was [[Headmaster]].<ref name=nc>{{cite web|title=Short History of Newington College |publisher=[[Newington College]] |url=http://www.newingtoncollege.nsw.edu.au/about/history.html |accessdate=11 February 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070901214518/http://www.newingtoncollege.nsw.edu.au/about/history.html |archivedate=1 September 2007 }}</ref> He is a BSc from the [[University of Sydney]],<ref name=usyd>{{cite web
  | title =Alumni Sidneienses
  | publisher =[[University of Sydney]]
  | url =https://alumniarchives.sydney.edu.au/as/FMPro?-db=as_main.fp5&-lay=web&-format=..%2Fas%2Fsearch_list.html&-max=10&-error=error.html&-SortField=dLastName&dLastName=Pyke&dFirstName=John&dGradYear=&-find=Go%21
  | accessdate = 17 February 2017}}</ref> an LLB from the [[University of New South Wales]] and an LLM from the University of Sydney.<ref name="qut"/>

==Career==
Pyke was a physicist for 15 years before studying law. He then taught law at the [[University of New South Wales]] and [[Macquarie University]] before moving to the [[Queensland University of Technology]] in 1983. He has taught Litigation, Land Law, Family Law, Contracts, Trade Practices, Introduction to Law, History and Philosophy of Law, Law in Context, Jurisprudence, Legal Research and Writing, Legal Institutions and Method, and a number of Constitutional Law subjects. Pyke's main interests lie in the fields of legal reasoning and constitutional law. Pyke has been a consultant to the now-defunct Electoral and Administrative Review Commission and to the independent member for [[Electoral district of Nicklin|Nicklin]], [[Peter Wellington]], on constitutional matters, and has made several submissions to Parliamentary Committees and to the Queensland Constitutional Review Commission. He is the QUT Law School’s coordinator of the Queensland Parliamentary Internship Program, under which students earn credit for doing research for a member or a committee of the [[Queensland Parliament]].<ref name=bio>{{cite web 
  | title =John Pyke - Biography 
  | publisher =[[Queensland University of Technology]] 
  | url =http://staff.qut.edu.au/staff/pyke/ 
  | accessdate =11 February 2012 
  | archive-date =2 February 2012 
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20120202000357/http://staff.qut.edu.au/staff/pyke 
  | url-status =dead 
  }}</ref>

==Political candidate==
In 2001 Pyke ran for election to the Senate on a Queensland ticket for [[Republican Party of Australia]]. At the 2010 Federal election Pyke campaigned for governments to impose stricter limits on the numbers of [[poker machine]]s allowed per State and for limits on the feed rate and to keep up the pressure on all governments to adopt the [[Productivity Commission]]'s recommendations, and progressively do more to reduce governments' dependence on gambling taxes.<ref name="qsc"/>
